provenance.note: Sabal palmetto (sabal palmetto) is the drawable stand-in for Cocos nucifera, the coconut palm that stands over almost every compound on the coastal plain; it is the only drawable single-trunk palm model of this height besides the Washingtonia. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the stand-in model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json, so placement matches what is drawn. Coconuts were grown in West Africa long before European contact but the species is native to the Indo-Pacific, so native_status is Introduced and the weight is set for an Introduced plant. community_weight is judgement, a relative share among the garden's trees.

provenance.note: Washingtonia filifera (California fan palm) is the drawable stand-in for Elaeis guineensis, the oil palm that surrounds Accra's smallholdings and gives pied crows and hornbills somewhere high to sit. The two models are the same size and archetype, so a compound with both palms reads correctly. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json. Elaeis guineensis is native to tropical Africa, so native_status is Native. community_weight is judgement and low, because an oil palm belongs on the boundary rather than over the yard.

provenance.note: Ilex opaca (American holly) is the drawable stand-in for Mangifera indica: a dense, round-crowned evergreen of about the size a garden mango reaches, and the model the simulation can draw that reads as an evergreen fruit tree. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json. The mango is native to South Asia, so native_status is Introduced and its weight is divided to match the importer's 0.3 multiplier for Introduced plants; the tree is the compound's main fruit tree, where the hornbill, plantain-eaters and fruit bats feed. community_weight is otherwise judgement.

provenance.note: Magnolia grandiflora (southern magnolia) is the drawable stand-in for Vitellaria paradoxa, the shea tree, which is an evergreen West African tree that keeps a dense crown and fruits after the rains. It is a large model, so the weight is low and the tree belongs at the boundary. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json. Vitellaria paradoxa is native to Africa, so native_status is Native. community_weight is judgement.

provenance.note: Tilia americana (American basswood) is the drawable stand-in for Milicia excelsa, the African teak, Ghana's famous timber tree and the tree the straw-coloured fruit bat is recorded as the main seed disperser of. Milicia is deciduous in the dry season and the basswood model is drawn deciduous, so the dry-season scene loses this tree honestly. Growth form, evergreen flag, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json. Milicia excelsa is native to tropical Africa, so native_status is Native. community_weight is judgement and low, because a teak is a boundary tree here, not a garden tree.

provenance.note: Carpinus caroliniana (American hornbeam) is the drawable stand-in for Theobroma cacao, the small understorey tree of a cocoa farm, at the height a cacao tree reaches in a compound. Growth form, height_m and crown_width_m are the model's, from schema/v0.1/flora-taxa.json. The model is drawn deciduous while a cacao tree is evergreen in life; the entry keeps the model's flag so the drawn tree matches its model, and this is the one mismatch a reviewer may want to weigh. Cacao was brought to West Africa from the Americas, so native_status is Introduced and the weight is set for an Introduced plant. community_weight is judgement.
